title: Registry finalization lock contention: concurrent lanes crash _persist_final_progress

Finalization should retry/backoff well past 30s or persist a fallback record outside the lock; a completed child's output must never be reported as failure because of registry contention. Observed 2026-08-26, ship-cleanup fleet.

title: capabilities refresh misreports fingerprint_mismatch as requested_harnesses_not_installed
description:
resolve_harness_selector returns fingerprint_mismatch (harness_discovery.py) when the configured binary answers as a different known harness. That collapses to installed: false, so `capabilities refresh`/`setup` tell the user the harness is missing when it is actually present and running under the wrong identity. Confirmed still true against current code: capability_commands.py's requested_harnesses_not_installed path only checks record.get("installed") is True, with no separate branch for fingerprint_mismatch, even though a probeStatus field now exists in the schema (capability_commands.py, describe_payload.py, model_discovery.py).

The honest fix needs probeStatus as a closed, schema-validated enum ({ok, partial, missing, error}) persisted in the cache, distinguishing "wrong harness" from "missing" — design-first, not a quick wording change. Precedent: the CONFIGURED_SELECTOR_MISSING vs probe_missing split already in harness_discovery.py.

Source: docs/plans/deferred.md, "Still open after the sweep" (2026-07-25 sweep record).

title: Discovery cache keyed on auth profile can ping-pong across invocation contexts
description:
An agent sandbox resolves e.g. `codex` to a cmux shim under TMPDIR; a login shell resolves the same auth profile to /opt/homebrew/bin/codex. Same profile, two answers, one cache file, so two contexts can each invalidate the other's record and ping-pong indefinitely. Masked today because drift comparison uses configured selectors rather than resolved paths, but any future move toward resolved-path comparison walks straight into it. Not yet designed.

Source: docs/plans/deferred.md, "Still open after the sweep" (2026-07-25 sweep record).

title: Mail tests break in shallow checkouts: tempdir at parents[3] of test file
description: tests/test_mail_*.py setUp creates its TemporaryDirectory at Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] — two levels above the repo root, deliberately outside the tree. In a checkout at depth 2 (e.g. a git worktree at /tmp/x) that resolves to / and every test fails with PermissionError, 30 failures that look environmental. Deep checkouts silently drop temp dirs into unrelated parent directories instead. Fix: walk up from the repo root to the first writable directory, or use a dedicated env-var override with a tmpfile fallback that is still outside the repo.

title: Design and ship explicit worktree reap deletion verb
description:
`worktree gc --all` (shipped v0.21.0) only scans and reports orphaned worktrees whose source repo is gone — it deletes nothing, at any depth, by design. The actual reclamation verb was deliberately deferred: a separate explicit `worktree reap --older-than DAYS --yes` command with real pool-root validation. This is the lesson from the round-1 review blocker on the original sweep: `--pool PATH` (arbitrary user root) composed with empty-dir rmdir meant `gc --pool "$HOME"` could have removed home directories — each piece was safe alone, so the deletion verb needs its own careful design pass, not a flag bolted onto gc.

Related caveats to fold into this design rather than opening separate tickets (per the deferred doc's own instruction): source_root_missing records are permanently visible/unclearable since deletion depends on a live source that creation didn't require; and `_has_detached_backlink` can mislabel a non-worktree directory nested under an unrelated ancestor repo — cosmetic today, becomes load-bearing once a reaper acts on classification.

Source: docs/plans/deferred.md, "Still open after the sweep" (2026-07-25 sweep record) + worktree gc fixes #3/#4 section (v0.18.0).
